detail.longDescription: So I have a script that can hide various id elements in a select drop-down based on a radio button. But it currently only hides one of the ids in the dropdown. How do I hide the others? I click on "Human", I want all the IDs that are NOT human to vanish. But it only vanishes the FIRST of each ID. So if I click "Human", it just removes "Demon 1", "Vampire 1" and "Werewolf 1". I need it to also remove "Demon 2", "Vampire 2" and "Werewolf 2" I'm using Javascript, running it from the browser. The code: var raceArray = ["Human", "Demon", "Vampire", "Werewolf"]; function species(z) { for (x = 0; x <4; x++) { //x<4 is actually x<raceArray.length var hide_race = document.getElementById(raceArray[x]); hide_race.hidden = true; } var show_race = document.getElementById(raceArray[z]); //Should show every option for whatever was selected. Even if it was previously hidden. show_race.hidden = false; } <input type="radio" onclick="species(0)" name="ruleset">Human <input type="radio" onclick="species(1)" name="ruleset">Demon <input type="radio" onclick="species(1)" name="ruleset">Vampire <input type="radio" onclick="species(2)" name="ruleset">Werewolf <select id="race"> <option id="Human">Human</option> <option id="Demon">Demon 1</option> <option id="Demon">Demon 2</option> <option id="Vampire">Vampire 1</option> <option id="Vampire">Vampire 2</option> <option id="Werewolf">Werewolf 1</option> <option id="Werewolf">Werewolf 2</option> </select> Edit: Added names to the radio buttons and changed .length to be 4 to be simpler. If need be, I can post the FULL code instead of a more simplified version.
